text: Ever felt your ears pop when a plane lands?
As the plane descends, the air pressure in the cabin rises.
But the air behind your eardrum may not adjust as quickly.
The higher pressure outside pushes your eardrum inward, making your ear feel blocked.
A narrow passage connects your middle ear to the back of your nose.
But when you swallow or yawn, tiny muscles briefly open it, letting air into your middle ear.
As the pressure balances, your eardrum can move more freely, and you may hear that little pop.
